question: Which of the following compounds is used in soda-acid fire extinguishers?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium bicarbonate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃) is used in soda-acid fire extinguishers.
 
• It reacts with sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄) to produce carbon dioxide (CO₂), which helps to extinguish the fire.
 
• The chemical reaction involved is: NaHCO₃ + H₂SO₄ → Na₂SO₄ + CO₂ + H₂O.
 
• The generated CO₂ gas forms a blanket over the fire, cutting off the oxygen supply and thereby extinguishing it.
 
• Sodium bicarbonate is preferred because it is non-flammable and non-toxic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bleaching powder**

 
 
• Also known as calcium hypochlorite, it is used for disinfecting drinking water and in the textile industry for bleaching.
 
• It is not used in fire extinguishers.
 
 
 
• **Calcium chloride**
 
 
• It is used for de-icing roads and in the food industry as a firming agent.
 
• It is not used in fire extinguishers.
 
 
 
• **Sodium carbonate**
 
 
• Commonly known as washing soda, it is used in glass manufacturing and as a water softener.
 
• It is not used in fire extinguishers.
